# Keeping order records: four years after each sale

Keep each order record for at least four years after the sale [1]. That is the State of Example's own period, and it is the one to plan around.

## What the statute says

The State of Example's statute requires a business selling to consumers to keep each order record for at least four years after the sale [1]. The official text is current through the 2026 regular session.

## Why not seven years

One compliance summary site says most states require seven years [2]. That figure is about states in general, not about this state, so we do not recommend it as your rule.

## What to do

We recommend keeping every order record for four years from the date of the sale. Orders over 4,000 need the owner's approval [3], so keep that approval note with the order record for the same four years.

## Sources

1. [State of Example statute, section 12-4-110](https://statutes.example.org/title-12/chapter-4/section-12-4-110), statutes.example.org, 22 October 2026.
2. [Records retention for small businesses](https://compliance-digest.example.net/records-retention-small-business), compliance-digest.example.net, 22 October 2026.
3. The owner's approval rule, Mossgate Books, 23 October 2026.
